meta.note: Stage 2: NCERT Exercises Q1–4 + Intext + concept bank. Activities 5.1–5.8 linked per day.

questions.question: The kidneys in human beings are a part of the system for
options: nutrition
respiration
excretion
transportation
questions.explanation: Kidneys filter blood and remove nitrogenous wastes (urea) as urine — part of the excretory system.

questions.question: The xylem in plants are responsible for
options: transport of water
transport of food
transport of amino acids
transport of oxygen
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels transport water and dissolved minerals from roots upward to leaves and other parts.

questions.question: Why is diffusion insufficient to meet the oxygen requirements of multicellular organisms like humans?
options: Multicellular organisms do not need oxygen
Most cells are not in direct contact with the environment
Diffusion is too fast for large bodies
Oxygen cannot diffuse through cell membranes
questions.explanation: In large organisms most cells are deep inside the body and too far from the surface for diffusion alone to supply O₂ quickly enough.

questions.question: Where does photosynthesis primarily occur in a green plant?
options: Roots
Green parts of the plant, especially leaves
Flowers only
Stem bark
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts in green parts (mainly mesophyll of leaves) carry out photosynthesis using chlorophyll.

questions.question: Which enzyme begins starch digestion in the human mouth?
options: Pepsin
Salivary amylase
Trypsin
Lipase
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) in saliva converts starch to maltose in the buccal cavity.

questions.question: Breathing and respiration are not the same because
options: Breathing is biochemical breakdown of glucose
Respiration is only inhaling and exhaling air
Breathing is ventilation; respiration releases energy from food in cells
They occur in different organisms
questions.explanation: Breathing moves air in and out of lungs; cellular respiration is the enzyme-controlled release of energy from glucose inside cells.

questions.question: Food synthesised in leaves is transported to other parts of the plant through
options: xylem
phloem
stomata
root hairs
questions.explanation: Phloem translocates sucrose and other food materials from source (leaves) to sink organs.

questions.question: The functional unit of the kidney that filters blood is the
options: alveolus
nephron
villus
stomata
questions.explanation: Each nephron consists of glomerulus, Bowman's capsule, tubules, and collecting duct — filters blood and forms urine.

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Why maintenance is needed**?
options: Small size + large surface area → diffusion works.
Special transport systems are needed in large bodies.
Maintenance needs energy from outside or from food
No energy needed for simple diffusion.
questions.explanation: Maintenance needs energy from outside or from food.
questions.category_label: Day 1 — Life Processes — Introduction · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Molecular movement and life**?
options: Food → energy + building blocks.
Life needs controlled movement of substances
Visible movement alone is not enough to prove life.
Nutrition → respiration → transport → excretion.
questions.explanation: Life needs controlled movement of substances.
questions.category_label: Day 1 — Life Processes — Introduction · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: The autotrophic mode of nutrition requires
options: carbon dioxide and water
chlorophyll
sunlight
all of the above
questions.explanation: Autotrophic nutrition (photosynthesis) needs CO₂, water, chlorophyll to trap light, and sunlight as energy source.

questions.question: The breakdown of pyruvate to give carbon dioxide, water and energy takes place in
options: cytoplasm
mitochondria
chloroplast
nucleus
questions.explanation: After glycolysis in cytoplasm, pyruvate enters mitochondria where it is completely oxidised aerobically to CO₂, H₂O, and ATP.

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Steps in holozoic nutrition**?
options: Food becomes part of body or fuel.
Egestion = undigested food out; excretion = metabolic waste.
Memorise order of five steps
Large molecules → small absorbable units.
questions.explanation: Memorise order of five steps.
questions.category_label: Day 5 — Heterotrophic Nutrition · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Ingestion**?
options: Food becomes part of body or fuel.
All depend on autotrophs directly or indirectly.
Mouth is start of alimentary canal
Memorise order of five steps.
questions.explanation: Mouth is start of alimentary canal.
questions.category_label: Day 5 — Heterotrophic Nutrition · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Heterotrophic nutrition — recap**?
options: Paramoecium has oral groove and gullet leading to food vacuole for digestion.
Assimilation is using absorbed nutrients for energy, growth, and repair.
Amoeba extends pseudopodia around food, forms food vacuole, digests with enzymes.
Organisms that cannot make their own food ingest complex organic matter and break it down.
questions.explanation: All depend on autotrophs directly or indirectly.
questions.category_label: Day 5 — Heterotrophic Nutrition · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Mouth and buccal cavity**?
options: Completes digestion started elsewhere.
Protein digestion begins in stomach.
Incisors cut, canines tear, molars grind
Most absorption also happens here.
questions.explanation: Incisors cut, canines tear, molars grind.
questions.category_label: Day 6 — Human Digestion — Upper Tract · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Saliva and salivary amylase**?
options: Emulsification increases lipase efficiency.
Churning mixes food with gastric juice.
Starch digestion begins in mouth
Most absorption also happens here.
questions.explanation: Starch digestion begins in mouth.
questions.category_label: Day 6 — Human Digestion — Upper Tract · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Human digestive system overview**?
options: Alimentary canal plus associated glands form the human digestive system.
Saliva moistens food and contains amylase (ptyalin) that starts starch digestion to maltose.
Teeth mechanically break food; tongue mixes and tastes; saliva begins chemical digestion.
Complete digestion of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats occurs in small intestine.
questions.explanation: Also: salivary glands, liver, pancreas.
questions.category_label: Day 6 — Human Digestion — Upper Tract · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Villi and microvilli**?
options: Huge surface area in folded wall
Know organ order and main function each.
Memorise four key enzymes.
Anus is exit for undigested residue.
questions.explanation: Huge surface area in folded wall.
questions.category_label: Day 7 — Human Digestion — Absorption · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Absorption in small intestine**?
options: Prevention is part of nutrition health.
Villi → capillaries → hepatic portal vein
Each enzyme works best at specific pH.
Huge surface area in folded wall.
questions.explanation: Villi → capillaries → hepatic portal vein.
questions.category_label: Day 7 — Human Digestion — Absorption · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Xylem — definition**?
options: Creates suction pulling water upward.
Dead cells form hollow tubes.
Roots absorb; leaves photosynthesise — connection needed.
One-way upward flow mainly
questions.explanation: One-way upward flow mainly.
questions.category_label: Day 11 — Transport in Plants — Xylem · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Phloem — definition**?
options: Creates suction pulling water upward.
Bidirectional food movement
Roots absorb; leaves photosynthesise — connection needed.
Water vapour from leaf condenses.
questions.explanation: Bidirectional food movement.
questions.category_label: Day 11 — Transport in Plants — Xylem · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Transport in plants — why needed**?
options: Place plant stem in eosin/coloured water; cut sections show dye in xylem vessels.
Plastic bag on leaf shows water droplets inside — proof of transpiration.
Xylem has vessels and tracheids — thick lignified walls, no cytoplasm in mature cells.
Plants need transport to move water, minerals, and food between roots, stem, and leaves.
questions.explanation: Roots absorb; leaves photosynthesise — connection needed.
questions.category_label: Day 11 — Transport in Plants — Xylem · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Translocation**?
options: Turgor pressure supports herbaceous plants.
Both are vascular tissues in plants.
Uses ATP at source loading
Plants regulate stomatal opening.
questions.explanation: Uses ATP at source loading.
questions.category_label: Day 12 — Transport in Plants — Phloem · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Source and sink**?
options: Turgor pressure supports herbaceous plants.
Adaptations match habitat.
Direction reverses seasonally in some plants
Active transport uses ATP from respiration.
questions.explanation: Direction reverses seasonally in some plants.
questions.category_label: Day 12 — Transport in Plants — Phloem · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Phloem tissue structure**?
options: Minerals enter root hairs by active transport against concentration gradient — needs energy.
Translocation is movement of food (sucrose) through phloem from source to sink.
Phloem has sieve tubes and companion cells; living cells transport dissolved sugars.
Xylem + transpiration pull for water up; phloem + translocation for food to all parts.
questions.explanation: Sieve plates allow flow between cells.
questions.category_label: Day 12 — Transport in Plants — Phloem · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Blood — components**?
options: Capillaries are one cell thick.
RBCs carry O₂; WBCs fight infection; platelets clot
Diffusion alone fails beyond tiny thickness.
Separates low-pressure lung circuit from high-pressure body.
questions.explanation: RBCs carry O₂; WBCs fight infection; platelets clot.
questions.category_label: Day 13 — Transport in Animals — Blood · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Plasma function**?
options: Too few platelets → bleeding risk.
Haemoglobin binds O₂ in lungs.
Part of immune system.
About 55% of blood volume
questions.explanation: About 55% of blood volume.
questions.category_label: Day 13 — Transport in Animals — Blood · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Transport in animals — need**?
options: Plasma transports digested food, CO₂, hormones, and waste products dissolved in water.
Platelets are cell fragments that help blood clot at injury sites.
Animals need circulatory system to deliver O₂, food, hormones and remove wastes from all cells.
Human heart drives double circulation — pulmonary and systemic circuits.
questions.explanation: Diffusion alone fails beyond tiny thickness.
questions.category_label: Day 13 — Transport in Animals — Blood · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Pulmonary circulation**?
options: Count beats per minute at rest.
Faulty valves cause murmurs.
Pulse points: wrist, neck.
Gas exchange in alveoli
questions.explanation: Gas exchange in alveoli.
questions.category_label: Day 14 — Heart and Circulation · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Egestion vs excretion vs secretion**?
options: Do not call urination egestion
Ureter connects kidney to bladder.
Lungs excrete CO₂ every breath.
Not the same as egestion or sweating alone.
questions.explanation: Do not call urination egestion.
questions.category_label: Day 15 — Excretion — Plants and Kidneys · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Excretion in plants**?
options: Do not call urination egestion.
Guttation exudes liquid water with salts.
Resins and gums are waste products
Nephron is functional unit of kidney.
questions.explanation: Resins and gums are waste products.
questions.category_label: Day 15 — Excretion — Plants and Kidneys · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Excretion — definition**?
options: Pair of kidneys filter blood to remove urea, excess water, and salts as urine.
Plants excrete O₂ (photosynthesis), CO₂ (respiration), water vapour, and store or drop wastes.
Day 16 covers nephron structure, filtration, and Activity 5.
Excretion is removal of harmful metabolic wastes produced in the body.
questions.explanation: Not the same as egestion or sweating alone.
questions.category_label: Day 15 — Excretion — Plants and Kidneys · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Nephron parts**?
options: Know at least four parts for exam
Proteins and RBCs not filtered.
Damage to nephrons impairs filtration.
All four needed continuously.
questions.explanation: Know at least four parts for exam.
questions.category_label: Day 16 — Nephron, Dialysis and Exam Prep · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Ultrafiltration in glomerulus**?
options: Proteins and RBCs not filtered
Damage to nephrons impairs filtration.
Comparison questions are common.
Transplant is long-term alternative.
questions.explanation: Proteins and RBCs not filtered.
questions.category_label: Day 16 — Nephron, Dialysis and Exam Prep · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Nephron — functional unit**?
options: When kidneys fail, dialysis machine removes urea from blood using semi-permeable membrane.
Nephron is the structural and functional unit of kidney — filters blood and forms urine.
Unit 1 Life Processes complete — 160 concept cards; proceed to Practice when unlocked.
Remaining fluid in collecting duct is urine — concentrated urea, excess water and salts.
questions.explanation: Damage to nephrons impairs filtration.
questions.category_label: Day 16 — Nephron, Dialysis and Exam Prep · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Diffusion in unicellular organisms**?
options: Maintenance needs energy from outside or from food.
Living things must carry out life processes continuously.
No energy needed for simple diffusion.
Small size + large surface area → diffusion works
questions.explanation: Small size + large surface area → diffusion works.
questions.category_label: Day 1 — Life Processes — Introduction · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Diffusion insufficient in multicellular organisms**?
options: Visible movement alone is not enough to prove life.
Nutrition → respiration → transport → excretion.
Special transport systems are needed in large bodies
Life needs controlled movement of substances.
questions.explanation: Special transport systems are needed in large bodies.
questions.category_label: Day 1 — Life Processes — Introduction · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **What are life processes?**?
options: Outside materials are used to build body structure and to provide energy for life processes.
In unicellular organisms, the entire surface is in direct contact with the environment — diffusion alone is enough.
Living organisms take in raw materials from outside: carbon-based food/CO₂, water, and inorganic salts.
Life processes are the basic functions performed by living organisms to maintain life — nutrition, respiration, transport, excretion, and more.
questions.explanation: Living things must carry out life processes continuously.
questions.category_label: Day 1 — Life Processes — Introduction · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Autotrophic nutrition**?
options: Decompose dead material; recycle nutrients.
Parasite benefits; host is harmed.
Photosynthesis in leaves; absorption by roots.
Make food from inorganic raw materials
questions.explanation: Make food from inorganic raw materials.
questions.category_label: Day 2 — Nutrition — Modes and Overview · Apply — examples and reasoning
